title: fix(driver-memory): make the `$contains` family case-exact and answer `count_distinct`
body:
Fixes #6814
Fixes #6682

Both cards' `driver-mongodb` halves landed earlier today (PR #7550, PR #7625). These are the `driver-memory` halves — the last open scope of each — so merging this closes both. Authorized by the maintainer's 2026-08-11 full lift of the #5499 freeze (#5499 comment `5252526378`).

After this, **`scripts/check-driver-conformance.mjs` reports `40 covered cell(s), 0 in the DEBT ledger, 0 exempt`** — the ledger is empty for the first time since the gate was written.

## Premise verified by EXECUTION before the first edit

Both suites were written first and run against unmodified `origin/main` @ `21888ab`:

| suite | pre-fix | post-fix |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `memory-filter-text-conformance.test.ts` | **9 failed / 43 passed** (52) | 52/52 |
| `memory-aggregation-conformance.test.ts` | **11 failed / 23 passed** (34) | 34/34 |

Every pre-fix failure in the text suite was a `$contains`-family row (`expected ['1','2'] to deeply equal ['2']`). Every `$icontains` row, every literal-comparand row, every refusal row and every reference-matcher row passed **before** the fix — which is what says the flag was the whole gap and that nothing was widened to reach green.

## #6682 — the `$contains` family, nine sites

The card framed this as "the query path + the analytics face". Measured, it is **nine `'i'`-flagged RegExp sites in three clusters**, and the third cluster is why the analytics face was wrong:

- `convertConditionToMongo` ~`:808-830` — the **AST spelling**'s four arms (`contains` / `notcontains` / `startswith` / `endswith`).
- `normalizeFieldOperators` ~`:985-994` — the **`$`-spelling**'s four arms. The dispatch flagged this cluster as possibly an `$in`-like path outside the ruling's reach; measured, it is the same four operators reached through the `FilterCondition` door, squarely inside #4706 Q2 = A. Nothing was widened beyond the family the ruling names.
- `filterSubstringPattern` `:1353` — the **#5374 shared rule**. The analytics face does not carry a fold of its own; it *borrows* this one. So one line fixed that face, which is the property #5374 bought, working in the direction it was built for.

`escapeRegex` is untouched (the comparand was always literal — that half was never the defect), and `$icontains` is untouched: its ASCII fold lives in the pattern *source* (`asciiCaseInsensitiveRegexSource`), not in a flag, so taking the flag off the family cannot move the boundary. A dedicated row asserts that.

## #6814 — `count_distinct`, and a premise the card got wrong

`MemoryDriver.computeAggregate` had arms for count/sum/avg/min/max and then `default: return null`. No `count_distinct` arm, so a function the Query Protocol declares and every SQL face lowers (#6409) resolved with `{ n: null }` — no error, no log, no refusal. It now returns `new Set(values.filter(v => v != null)).size`, the same expression `in-memory-aggregation.ts` uses.

**The card, the ledger row and `aggregation-conformance.ts`'s DEBT table all read the ANALYTICS face as the one that "DOES implement `count_distinct`". Executing the case-set falsified that.** `buildAggregator` emitted `{ $addToSet }` under a comment reading *"Will need post-processing for count"* — and no post-processing existed. So the measure answered the raw **array** of values, `['won','lost',null]`, under a field `measureTypeToFieldType` describes as `number`.

One declared function, three answers: `null` on the data face, an array on the analytics face, and the standard's number nowhere. Both are fixed here, the array sized excluding null — the same exclusion the driver-mongodb half made on `$addToSet` (#7550).

## Multi-face declaration (per face of THIS package)

| face | `$contains` family | `count_distinct` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **query path** (`memory-driver.ts`, both spellings, both doors of `find()`/`aggregate(AST)`) | **fixed here** — 8 sites | **fixed here** — the missing arm |
| **analytics face** (`memory-analytics.ts`) | **fixed here** — via `filterSubstringPattern`, the shared rule it borrows | **fixed here** — `$addToSet` sized, null-excluded |
| **reference matcher** (`memory-matcher.ts`) | **already compliant** — `String.includes`, case-exact all along; verified by 13 rows in the new suite, file untouched | n/a — not an aggregate face |

The cross-backend scoreboard is settled and not re-proved here (#6518 / #7625).

## Out of scope, with reason

**#7117 (`memory-analytics.ts` `generateSql` / `operatorToSql`).** The sweep did pass through it: `contains` renders as `LIKE`, which folds ASCII on a SQLite-shaped consumer. It is **not fixed here**, and this is a judgement rather than an omission — making it case-exact means choosing `GLOB` or a binary cast per dialect, and the pattern that construct takes is exactly the wildcard rendering #7117 owns. A half-change would emit incoherent SQL. This exit is also descriptive (it returns SQL text, it does not execute it), so no row set moves. Reported as adjacency; #7117 is deliberately serialized behind this card.

**`memory-analytics.ts`'s cube `count` measure** emits `{ $sum: 1 }` regardless of `sql`, i.e. `count(*)` semantics — the shape whose driver-side twin #7550 fixed on mongodb. Not touched: `measureToSql` emits `COUNT(*)` for the same measure, so that face is self-consistent, and cube `count` semantics are a different question from `AGGREGATION_CASES`' `count(col)`. Recorded so it is not rediscovered as a defect.

## Pins flipped, never deleted

Five assertions encoded the fold. All five flipped to the ruled substance:

- `memory-driver.test.ts` — `should filter with $contains case-insensitively` → `case-SENSITIVELY` (asserts 0 rows for `'alice'`, 1 for `'Alice'`), **plus a new sibling** pinning `$icontains` so the pair still covers both behaviours rather than losing one.
- `memory-driver.test.ts` — `$contains inside $and`: the subject is *combination*, so the comparand moved rather than the expectation (`'a'` matched `Alice Johnson` only through the fold). `'o'` is case-exact for both rows and makes the conjunction do visible work.
- `memory-driver-filter-logic-conformance.test.ts` — the three `#5374` case rows now assert the family is case-SENSITIVE *on both faces*, **plus a positive control** so they cannot be passed by a predicate that stopped matching anything.

## Reverse verification — direction predicted before it was run

Recorded in the aggregation suite's docblock, both reverts executed:

- **(A) the `count_distinct` arm removed** — predicted failures on the VALUE `null`, never a throw, arithmetic cases green. Measured **7 failed / 27 passed**, exactly that.
- **(B) the arm present but `new Set(values).size`** — null not excluded. Predicted 3-for-2 ungrouped and `east` 2 / `west` 3 grouped, with `count_distinct(score)` staying GREEN at 6. Measured **6 failed / 28 passed**, exactly that. (B) is unreachable by a suite that only tests one column, which is why the table carries both.

## Prose this PR makes false, corrected

Four files carried claims the diff falsifies. All prose/docblock only — zero schema or behaviour lines:

- `packages/spec/src/data/filter-text-conformance.ts` — the status list and one case note.
- `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts` — the `$contains`-family status paragraph and the DEBT-row sentence.
- `packages/spec/src/data/aggregation-conformance.ts` — the DEBT table (driver-memory enrolled; the "analytics face agrees" row corrected to what execution showed) and the enrolled-backends list.
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx` — two `warn` callouts saying one driver still folds, now `info` and naming the row-set change for anyone who relied on it.

## Gates

| gate | result |
|:--|:--|
| `check:driver-conformance` | **OK — 40 covered, 0 DEBT, 0 exempt** |
| `check:driver-conformance --self-test` | OK |
| driver-memory suite | 664 passed (22 files) |
| `@objectstack/spec` suite | 9883 passed (377 files) |
| `@objectstack/objectql` suite | 3228 passed (182 files) |
| `@objectstack/runtime` suite | 2018 passed (127 files) |
| service-datasource / http-conformance / verify | 326 / 72 / 23 passed |
| `tsc --noEmit` (driver-memory, spec) | clean |
| build (driver-memory dependency closure) | clean |

Downstream selection was measured, not assumed: `pnpm --filter '...@objectstack/driver-memory'` lists 16 dependents; `objectql` is **not** among them (it depends the other way), so its suite was run on its own account and is green.

Changeset: `.changeset/memory-contains-case-and-count-distinct.md`, **patch** for `@objectstack/driver-memory` — a user-visible row-set change on the `$contains` family plus `count_distinct` now answering, telling anyone relying on the fold to write `$icontains`.

No `content/docs/releases/` edit.
